newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: New Congo troops search opposition faction for arms.
newsitem.headline: New Congo troops search opposition faction for arms.

text.p: Troops searched the house of the leader of an opposition faction in the Democratic Republic of Congo for weapons on Friday but said the group had not been keeping arms.
Witnesses earlier said both the soldiers and bodyguards of political faction leader, Kibassa Maliba, had fired in the air. They said two bodyguards were arrested after being found with arms.
"Those people were innocent, there was nothing there," said the commander of the military unit that carried out the search.
He said one gun had been found in the back garden and confiscated, but added that it appeared to have been thrown over the fence from outside.
Kibassa broke away from veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi's Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party in 1996 and moved closer to ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko.

Several hundred of Tshisekedi's supporters on Friday marched through Kinshasa to protest against newly-installed President Laurent Kabila and the presence of Rwandan troops among his forces who drove Mobutu out almost two weeks ago.

Soldiers of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo allowed the demonstrators to march as far as Tshisekedi's house, which is only a few hundred metres (yards) from Kibassa's residence.
Witnesses said Tshisekedi's supporters later moved toward Kibassa's house where they taunted his bodyguards and encouraged Alliance troops to search the building.

"There were no weapons. The Tshisekedi supporters after their failed march came and attacked us throwing stones. They told the soldiers that we had arms and after a search they found nothing," Ewanga Jean-Bertrand, spokesman for Kibassa's faction of the UDPS, told Reuters.
